## Step 1, partially answered — read on the cloud tree (`3856fbf7`), read-only

The maintainer opened the cloud repository for this reading. Two facts established, one decisive fact still open.

### ✅ Established 1 — the real `@objectstack/organizations` does NOT patch this hole

`cloud/packages/organizations/src` contains exactly: `organizations-plugin.ts`, `ensure-default-organization.ts`, `multi-org-license-gate.ts`, `membership-policy-gate.ts`, `claim-org-seed-ownership.ts`, `claim-orphan-org-rows.ts`, `manifest.ts`, `index.ts`.

A grep across all of it for `api_key` / `apiKey` / `accessible_org_ids` / `authRefusal` / `membership_ended` / `resolveAuthzContext` returns **no request-time admission code** — only `resolveTenancyPosture` inside the two **boot** gates (license, membership policy). The plugin registers itself as the `org-scoping` service (activating the posture, ADR-0081 D2) and refuses to boot on undeclared policy; it performs **no per-request vetting of an API key's stamped organization**.

⇒ The probe's stand-in was behaviourally faithful for this question. **The enterprise plugin adds no refusal the open-core reading missed.**

### ✅ Established 2 — cloud DOES register a `kernel-manager` in production

`cloud/packages/objectos-runtime/src/objectos-stack.ts` — `ctx.registerService('kernel-manager', kernelManager)`, beside `env-registry`, `kernel-resolver` and `artifact-api-client`. Not a test fixture. That is the precondition the CONTROL arm needed.

### ⛔ Still open, and it is the fact that decides the blast radius

**Registration is not sufficient.** The measurement's KM-ONLY arm registered a `kernel-manager` and still behaved **byte-identically to the leaking SUBJECT arm**, because `kernel` never became *bound* in `computeExecCtx`. The trigger is binding, not presence.

So the remaining question is narrow and concrete: **on an objectos-ee data request, does `kernel` actually bind?** The architecture suggests yes — requests resolve an environment through `kernel-resolver`, which is the whole point of the per-environment kernel — but ⛔ that is an inference, and this card has already cost one inference (B′'s) that measured false. Routes that resolve no environment (control-plane surfaces) are the obvious place where it may not bind.

⇒ **Do not size this card, and do not rule on questions 1–3, until that is measured.** Two outcomes:

- `kernel` binds on data requests ⇒ blast radius is **open-core self-hosters**; cloud's own deployments are on the refusing side, and the repair is still owed but is not a live production leak.
- `kernel` does not bind on some reachable data path ⇒ blast radius is **every walled deployment**, cloud included.

Dispatching that measurement in the cloud repository now; its result lands here.

os-dev-report

## Verdict: OUTCOME 2 — `kernel` is NEVER bound on the shipped objectos-ee wiring, and cloud is on the EXPOSED side

Measured, not inferred: two real `objectstack serve` boots of `apps/objectos-ee` under a live
`isolated` posture, licensed, with the **real cloud-private `@objectstack/organizations`** mounted —
not the `SimulatedOrgScopingPlugin` stand-in #15163 had to use. On both, an API key stamped with an
organization its owner is no longer a member of **reads that organization's rows and writes a new row
into it**. HTTP 200 / HTTP 201, byte-identical to #15163's SUBJECT arm.

So the scope limit #15163 flagged is now closed in the worse direction: **the real enterprise plugin
adds no refusal.** Blast radius is every walled deployment, not just open-core self-hosters.

## The matrix — `GET` and `POST` on `/api/v1/data/sys_business_unit`, key in `x-api-key`

| credential | ARM A · shipped single-environment | ARM B · composed artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no credential | GET 401 · POST 401 | GET 401 |
| unknown key | GET 401 | — |
| member of `org_alpha` (positive control) | GET 200 total 2 · POST 201 | GET 200 total 2 · POST 201 |
| **ex-member, key stamped `org_alpha`** | **GET 200 total 3** · **POST 201, row lands `org_alpha`** | **GET 200 total 3** · **POST 201, row lands `org_alpha`** |
| org-less key | GET 200 **total 0** (silent) · POST 403 | GET 200 total 0 · POST 403 |

Raw, ARM A:

```
{"op":"GET","label":"no credential","http":401,"code":"UNAUTHENTICATED"}
{"op":"POST","label":"no credential","http":401,"code":"UNAUTHENTICATED"}
{"op":"GET","label":"member key [+control]","http":200,"total":2,"ids":["bu_a1","bu_a2"],"orgs":["org_alpha"]}
{"op":"POST","label":"member key [+control]","http":201,"id":"wvPt89YwyakCmhr_","org":"org_alpha"}
{"op":"GET","label":"EX-MEMBER key","http":200,"total":3,"ids":["bu_a1","bu_a2","wvPt89YwyakCmhr_"],"orgs":["org_alpha"]}
{"op":"POST","label":"EX-MEMBER key","http":201,"id":"P6X5yYS3AIzB-wOL","org":"org_alpha"}
{"op":"GET","label":"org-less key","http":200,"total":0,"ids":[],"orgs":[]}
{"op":"POST","label":"org-less key","http":403,"code":"PERMISSION_DENIED"}
{"op":"GET","label":"unknown key","http":401,"code":"UNAUTHENTICATED"}
```

Note the ex-member's `total 3`: it includes `wvPt89YwyakCmhr_`, the row the **legitimate member wrote
seconds earlier**. This is live cross-organization read, not just seed data.

## The write, read back FROM THE STORE — not from the response body

Server stopped, then the sqlite file opened directly with `node:sqlite`:

```
{"id":"bu_a1","organization_id":"org_alpha","created_by":null,"name":"alpha unit 1"}
{"id":"bu_a2","organization_id":"org_alpha","created_by":null,"name":"alpha unit 2"}
{"id":"bu_b1","organization_id":"org_beta","created_by":null,"name":"beta unit 1"}
{"id":"bu_b2","organization_id":"org_beta","created_by":null,"name":"beta unit 2"}
{"id":"wvPt89YwyakCmhr_","organization_id":"org_alpha","created_by":"u_member","name":"w-member"}
{"id":"P6X5yYS3AIzB-wOL","organization_id":"org_alpha","created_by":"u_exmember","name":"w-exmember"}
```

The last row is the ex-member's write, stamped `org_alpha`, in an organization `u_exmember` has no
`sys_member` row for. ARM B produced the same row (`xb4qFipiu52jyHiW`).

## Both positive controls hold, and a third one falls out of the fixture

1. **Data reaches.** The healthy member's key returns 200 with two records on the same route. A probe
   that cannot show data reaching has measured nothing; this one shows it.
2. **The door refuses when it should.** No credential is 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, and so is an unknown
   key.
3. **Layer 0 is live and the principal is not exempt.** The fixture seeds two rows in `org_beta` as
   well, and the member key never sees them — GET returns `["bu_a1","bu_a2"]`, never `bu_b1`/`bu_b2`.
   A platform-admin caller (the one principal `tenant-layer.ts` lets cross the wall) would have seen
   all four. And the org-less key's POST 403 shows a Layer 0 refusal IS reachable on this deployment.
   So the wall is enforced — and enforcing it is exactly what admits the ex-member, precisely as
   #15163 argued.

## How the boot was composed

`apps/objectos-ee`, driven exactly the way `test/serve-walled-posture.e2e.test.ts` drives it: plain
`node node_modules/@objectstack/cli/bin/run.js serve objectstack.config.ts`, `NODE_PATH` deleted,
`NODE_ENV=production`, ready detected on stdout+stderr combined.

```
OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated  OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only
OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL=platform-owner@objectos-ee.test  OS_AI_STUDIO_AGENTS=ask,build
OS_LICENSE_KEY=(ed25519-signed, offline, enterprise)  OS_DATABASE_URL=file:...
```

Boot banner:

```
Mode:    production
Driver:  SqlDriver(better-sqlite3)  -> file:.../measure.db
Tenancy: isolated
Plugins: 44 loaded
         ObjectQL, SqlDriver, HonoServer, PlatformObjects, Auth, @objectstack/setup,
         @objectstack/account, Organizations, Security, Audit,
         com.objectstack.security.enterprise, ...
```

`Organizations` there is the real `packages/organizations` — the walled-posture license gate and the
membership-policy gate both fired on the way up, so the enterprise multi-org runtime is genuinely in
the request path. `OS_DATABASE_URL` points at a FILE rather than `:memory:` precisely so written rows
can be read back from the store.

**Fixture.** `sys_business_unit` — a plain platform object carrying `organization_id` and no domain
guard of its own. Two rows in `org_alpha`, two in `org_beta`. `u_member` has a `sys_member` row for
`org_alpha`; `u_exmember` has one for `org_beta` ONLY, and its key is stamped `active_organization_id
= org_alpha`. RBAC is opened SYMMETRICALLY for all three principals through one `sys_permission_set`
carrying `viewAllRecords`/`modifyAllRecords` — the Layer 1 superuser bypass, which by `tenant-layer.ts`
does NOT cross Layer 0. So RBAC cannot be what separates the arms; only the organization wall can.

`sys_comment` was the first candidate and was DISCARDED, not worked around: it carries its own
`thread_id` guard (`RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`) and answered `total 0` for everyone, which would have
been a broken probe wearing the costume of a refusal.

## Requirement 4 — where does no environment resolve, and can a stamped key reach it?

On ARM A and ARM B the answer is stronger than "some path": **every** data path leaves `kernel`
unbound, because no `kernel-manager` is registered at all. Both of `computeExecCtx`'s kernel-binding
branches are guarded on `this.kernelManager`, so neither can be entered under any request shape —
URL-scoped, hostname-routed, header-scoped or bare. Confirmed behaviourally on both boots:

```
ARM A - shipped single-environment: boot=ready
  "registered env-registry + kernel-manager + kernel-resolver" present: false
  any "kernel-manager" mention at all: false
  plugins: 44   Organizations plugin mounted: true
ARM B - composed artifact: boot=ready
  "registered env-registry + kernel-manager + kernel-resolver" present: false
  any "kernel-manager" mention at all: false
  plugins: 45   Organizations plugin mounted: true
```

Census over the cloud tree — the ONE registrar, and neither shipped arm reaches it:

```
$ git grep -n "kernel-manager" -- packages/** apps/** plugins/** | grep register
packages/objectos-runtime/src/objectos-stack.ts:451:  ctx.registerService('kernel-manager', kernelManager);
```

`apps/objectos-ee/objectstack.config.ts` reaches `createObjectOSStack` only in its
`else if (cloudUrl)` branch, and `cloudUrl` is `undefined` unless `OS_MULTI_TENANT` is truthy
(`objectstack.config.ts:967-968`). The shipped default and the composed-artifact shape both take
other branches.

## ARM C — the multi-tenant shell: COULD NOT BOOT HERE, and exactly why

`OS_MULTI_TENANT=1` is the arm that mounts `createObjectOSStack` and therefore registers
`kernel-manager` + `env-registry` + `kernel-resolver` — the same shell `apps/objectos` and
`apps/cloud` build (`apps/objectos/objectstack.config.ts:55`). I could not boot it in this
environment. The exact failure, from the real `serve` child:

```
  x [driver-memory] Refusing to start: this driver has NO row-level tenant isolation.
  Detected: tenancy posture `isolated` - a multi-tenant deployment
```

Cause: `createHostEnginePlugins()` (`packages/objectos-runtime/src/objectos-stack.ts:196-203`)
hardcodes `new InMemoryDriver()` for the HOST kernel, and the framework's split-brain guard refuses
that driver under a walled posture. `OS_DATABASE_URL` does not reach it — the host kernel is a
routing shell (`MetadataPlugin({ registerSystemObjects: false })`) with a fixed driver, so there is
no knob to point it elsewhere. Tried, in order: with `dist/objectstack.json` absent; then with the
artifact built via `objectstack build` (the artifact declares no `datasources`, so
`extractRuntimeFromMetadata` yields nothing and the per-env fallback never gets a chance to matter,
because the refusal is the HOST kernel's and fires before any environment is requested).

⛔ I am NOT substituting a stand-in for that arm. What I can say without measuring is only what the
code says, and I flag it as unmeasured: that host kernel registers no system objects and owns no
tenant data, so an unscoped request there has no `sys_api_key` table to authenticate against. Whether
that makes the hosted SaaS safe is exactly the thing I did not measure, and it should not be assumed.

## Tree currency

Cloud measured at `512e4e61`, which IS today's `origin/main`. Every file the reading depends on is
byte-identical:

```
$ git diff --stat HEAD origin/main -- apps/objectos-ee/objectstack.config.ts packages/organizations/src \
    packages/objectos-runtime/src/objectos-stack.ts packages/objectos-runtime/src/kernel-resolver.ts \
    packages/objectos-runtime/src/artifact-environment-registry.ts \
    packages/objectos-runtime/src/file-artifact-api-client.ts
(no output)
```

Framework: measured against cloud's actual pin, `.objectstack-sha = 8a96e666` (the rig-pin checkout
at that SHA, dists built there), not against a moving local `main`. That pin is unchanged on today's
cloud `origin/main`.

## ⚠️ One thing the pin diff turned up, and it bears on the repair

Framework `origin/main` (`460134af8`) has already MOVED this seam since `8a96e666` — 109 insertions in
`rest-server.ts`, all in the posture block. It is the #13906 decision-1-option-A change: the read is
now guarded `if (kernel && typeof kernel.getServiceAsync === 'function')` and a tenancy service that
FAILED TO BUILD raises rather than admits. **The single-kernel branch still derives no posture**, so a
pin bump does not close what I measured.

Its own comment says why, and names a remedy that is not there:

> That path carries no posture at all; its half of this ruling (decision 1 option B-prime) is refused
> at BOOT instead — see `rest-api-plugin.ts`.

`rest-api-plugin.ts` on `origin/main` carries no such refusal (that is PR #15020, withdrawn
2026-09-04). So on framework main the load-bearing comment on a p0 seam now points at a remedy that
was pulled, and the single-kernel half is documented as covered when it is not. Reported here rather
than filed separately, because it is this card's seam and this card's decision.

## What this settles for the three coupled questions

Question 1 (re-open the declined option) is no longer "how wide is this" — the cloud reading was the
gate on sizing it, and it came back exposed. Question 2 keeps its force unchanged: with `authRefusal`
still consumerless, deriving the posture alone converts this into a 401 byte-identical to sending no
credential, which is exactly what the `no credential` and `unknown key` rows above already look like.

⛔ Nothing was changed, committed or pushed. Probes were throwaway and are not in any tree.

## Maintainer ruling — **1A · 2A · 3A** (2026-09-04, decision batch #33): the single-kernel wiring derives the tenancy posture; the refusal is said on the server side and the wire stays a generic 401; the admit-on-unknown default stays, pinned unreachable on every shipped wiring

Director seat (objectstack #12708, summon 14, session_01LsEjuNMPitCHwEfYftZ1um, GitHub `os-warren`). Provenance: maintainer, live chat with the director seat, replying to batch #33 (this card alone, presented ~07:4xZ with the recommendation `1A · 2A · 3A`, cloud reading in parallel and not as a precondition). Verbatim: 「同意」.

**Sizing, now measured rather than open.** Between presentation and ruling the direct-dispatch channel landed the cloud reading here (5537399728 · 5537686722, cloud `512e4e61`, real `@objectstack/organizations` mounted): **outcome 2** — `kernel` is never bound on the shipped objectos-ee wiring (no `kernel-manager` registered on ARM A or ARM B), the enterprise plugin adds no request-time refusal, and the ex-member key reads and writes `org_alpha` with the row read back from the store. Blast radius is **every walled deployment**, cloud included; the multi-tenant shell (ARM C) could not be booted there and is unmeasured. The ruling below does not change with that reading; the release posture does (see the last section).

### Ruled

**1A — re-open and take the option declined on 2026-09-02.** `computeExecCtx`'s single-kernel branch derives the posture the way it already obtains `authService`: a provider wired by `rest-api-plugin` to the lone local kernel's `tenancy` service (same shape as `authServiceProvider`), evaluated under decision-1 option A's semantics — not registered ⇒ no posture; registered and failing ⇒ `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` (503), never a quiet absence. B′ (boot refusal) stays withdrawn per the maintainer's 04:14Z ruling on #13906.

**2A — the refusal is observable to operators, on the server side; the wire stays the generic 401.** `resolveAuthzContext` logs, at `warn`, at the point it decides each posture-conditional refusal (`organization_required` at admission, `organization_membership_ended` after grants): key id (never the secret), principal, organization, reason. The response body is unchanged (`401 UNAUTHENTICATED`) — no reason reaches a caller, so a holder of someone else's key learns nothing the generic 401 does not say. **#14273's A1 ruling stands unchanged**: the zero-reader `authRefusal` field is still removed by that card; the log line is the operator exit that field never delivered. Cross-referenced there.

**3A — the admit-on-unknown default stays, and its justification is rewritten.** `api-key.ts` keeps admitting an organization-less key when no posture is supplied. Its docblock's premise (a "transport not yet wired" residue) is false and is replaced by the only legitimate remaining case: a host that registers no `tenancy` service. The reachability pin makes "unknown" unreachable on every shipped wiring.

### Scope for the `domain:cli` seat — p0, one PR, before the 17.3 tag

1. `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts` + `rest-server.ts`: the posture provider on the single-kernel branch (1A). Fix the load-bearing comment in the posture block that still points at the withdrawn B′ boot refusal in `rest-api-plugin.ts` (the cloud reading found it: framework `main` documents the single-kernel half as covered when it is not).
2. `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`: the two `warn` lines (2A). Cross-lane touch of the engine lane's file **authorised by this ruling for this PR only** (the #14937 precedent); the `domain:engine` seat adopts on the card, no second PR. ⛔ Do not add the log inside `api-key.ts`'s admission path twice — one line per refusal, where the decision is made.
3. `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts`: the docblock rewrite (3A). No behaviour change.
4. Pins: (a) `execctx-authz-input-seam-reachability.test.ts` (or its successor) asserts that **every** `computeExecCtx` branch supplies a posture when a `tenancy` service is registered — the single-kernel branch included; (b) the #15163 matrix as a REST-level test on the single-kernel wiring under `isolated`: member 200/201, ex-member 401/401, organization-less 401, no credential 401, with the `warn` line asserted for the two refusals; (c) the ablation: remove the provider, the ex-member row goes back to 200 — quoted in the PR body.
5. **Census the other seven `resolveAuthzContext` callers** (mcp plugin, runtime `resolve-execution-context`, plugin-sharing, service-datasource admin routes, service-settings, service-storage, cloud-connection marketplace-install): which of them supply `tenancyPosture` today. #15163 measured REST only. A caller that can carry an API key and supplies no posture is the same hole through another door — fix in this PR if it is one line per site, else file per site with `Blocked-by:` and say so in the body. This is the confidence gap the maintainer was told about.
6. Changeset: `@objectstack/rest` **patch** and `@objectstack/core` **patch** — a fail-closed bug fix with no accept-set change and no new public surface (Clause-② **no**; the runtime authorization behaviour change is the human floor, and this ruling is that control). The changeset names the observable change: an organization-less or ex-member API key on a walled single-kernel deployment now answers 401 where it answered 200.
7. Not this PR's: the multi-tenant shell (ARM C) measurement in cloud; #14273's field removal (its own PR, A1); the `os serve` `--dev` host-config paths beyond the provider.

### State and follow-ups

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (read-modify-write; `bug` · `priority:p0` · `security` · `domain:cli` untouched). The parallel cloud card the director seat filed at 08:1xZ (#15279) is closed as superseded by 5537686722 — the reading exists. **Release posture is the maintainer's call and is put to them in chat, not ruled here:** with cloud on the exposed side, whether the fix ships as an out-of-band patch release with an advisory or rides 17.3. Ledger: objectstack #12708, batch #33 entry.

## ⭐ The premise changed while the dispatch was dying: **17.3.0 shipped**

`@objectstack/cli@17.3.0` and its siblings are tagged. Verified on `origin/main`: the single-kernel branch still derives no posture, and `rest-server.ts` still documents the seam as "refused at BOOT — see `rest-api-plugin.ts`" while that file carries no such refusal. **So the leak is in a released version**, not merely on `main`.

Consequences for this card, and only these:

- The ruling's "before the 17.3 tag" framing is spent. The scope, the three options and every ⛔ in the ruling are **unchanged** — it is the release vehicle that moved, and that is the maintainer's call, put to them in chat and ⛔ not decided here.
- The changeset stays `@objectstack/rest` patch + `@objectstack/core` patch as ruled. ⛔ Do not re-price it upward on account of the release having happened.

State: `pm:dispatched` and the assignee are retained through the takeover (the work is continuous). Session `6679d191-11f4-465b-b322-0e0409d76793`, maintainer direct-dispatch channel.

This card closed as completed by its `Fixes` line.

**Against the ruling, item by item:**

The stale comment that claimed the seam was "refused at BOOT" is gone — **paraphrased, not quoted**, so it no longer answers a grep for the withdrawn remedy, with a pin forbidding the phrase's return. Repo-wide the phrase now occurs exactly once, inside that regex.
- **2A** — one `warn` per refusal at the point it is decided, naming key id / principal / organization / reason; the wire stays `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, asserted by a test that the body matches none of `membership|organization_membership_ended|org_alpha|key_exmember`, and that neither the raw key nor its hash appears in the line. An unknown key produces **no** line — outcome `none` is not a refusal.
- **3A** — `api-key.ts` keeps admitting on an unknown posture; only the docblock changed, its false "transport not yet wired" premise replaced.
- **Pins and ablation** — verified by this seat in the test source, not taken from the report. The ablation is a **wiring** ablation held permanently in the test (`omitTenancyProvider: true` omits exactly the one constructor argument this card adds), so there is no mutated tree and no restore leg that can silently fail: with the provider omitted the ex-member reads (GET 200, total 2) and writes again (POST 201, row read back **from the store** as `org_alpha` / `u_exmember`); with it wired, 401/401 and nothing lands. Controls in both directions: a current member still reads and writes, no credential is still 401, and `org_beta`'s rows are never served.
